clue.text: Mark finds nothing in Kent, rambling

indicators.note: the word nothing is placed inside the scrambled county name
rambling means wandering about, so the letters of Kent wander into a new order

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone discovers no mark at all while out walking in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rambling' turns KENT into TKEN, and 'in' puts O (nothing) inside it after the T. Kent is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A token is a sign or symbol, which is one sense of mark.

clue.text: Highest standing champion gunfighter?

parts.note: top means best or champion, as in top dog
a gunfighter draws his gun, so he is a drawer

explanation.surface: Asks whether the best gunslinger in the West enjoys the highest reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful sense of drawer: one who draws a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-drawer is an idiom for first-class, of the highest social or quality rank.

clue.text: Nail-hardener a tinker employed

indicators.note: employed means put to use, so the letters of these two words are used to make something new

explanation.surface: A travelling mender is hired to strengthen nails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'employed' signals that the seven letters of A TINKER are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Keratin is the fibrous protein that makes fingernails hard.

clue.text: Green sodium provided that

parts.note: Na is the chemical symbol for sodium
if means on condition that, provided that

explanation.surface: A chemistry condition: green sodium, as long as that holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Naif means naive or inexperienced, the sense of green for a novice.

clue.text: Can attack butter on the farm

parts.note: a billy or billycan is a camping can for boiling water
to go at someone is to attack them

explanation.surface: A tin goes for some dairy produce down on the farm.
explanation.walkthrough: GO AT (attack) is written as one word GOAT; 'butter' is not the spread but one who butts.
explanation.definitionFit: A male goat is famous for ramming with its horns, so it is one that butts on a farm.

clue.text: Dorset-York leg difficult for the aristocratic swinger

indicators.note: difficult suggests the letters are troublesome and must be worked into another order

explanation.surface: A tricky stage of a journey between Dorset and York, for some noble swinger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'difficult' rearranges the thirteen letters of DORSET, YORK and LEG. Lord Greystoke is the title of Tarzan, who swings through the jungle on vines.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarzan, the vine-swinging jungle hero, was born heir to the noble title of Greystoke.

clue.text: Bitter, perhaps, after year in university

indicators.note: after places the beer type behind the year abbreviation

parts.note: bitter is a type of ale, the perhaps marking an example

explanation.surface: A drink of bitter after a year spent at university.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a British style of beer, so it is an example of ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Yale is an Ivy League university in Connecticut, an example of the class.

clue.text: One who stands up to problem at work?

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
a poser is a puzzling problem

explanation.surface: Someone who confronts a difficulty arising in the workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who resists or opposes something stands up to it.

clue.text: Lifting the foot that is shorter

parts.note: FT is the abbreviation, the shortened form, of foot

explanation.surface: Raising the foot that is the shorter one of a pair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is shorter' tells you to abbreviate foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting is slang for stealing, as in shoplifting.

clue.text: Average family at Garsdale Head leaving car

parts.note: par is the normal or average standard
kin means family or relations

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An ordinary family at the top of Garsdale abandon their car.
explanation.walkthrough: Garsdale is a dale in the Yorkshire Dales; only its first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Parking is stopping and leaving a vehicle somewhere.

clue.text: August newspaper featuring racing competition

parts.note: august means grand or majestic
a national is a newspaper sold across the whole country

explanation.surface: A distinguished paper sponsoring a race meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'August' is an adjective meaning grand, not the month. The Grand National is a famous British steeplechase at Aintree.
explanation.definitionFit: The best-known British steeplechase horse race, run at Aintree each spring.

clue.text: Rex asleep, but restless, taking a turn for worse

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: restless means unable to keep still, so the letters move about

explanation.surface: A dog called Rex sleeps fitfully and then falls ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rex' looks like a dog's name in the surface, but it is the Latin for king, abbreviated R; 'restless' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A relapse is a deterioration after partial recovery from illness.

clue.text: Girl in routine job at hospital

parts.note: a rut is a dull routine one is stuck in
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A young woman doing humdrum work at a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female first name, here standing for any girl.

clue.text: Reading between the lines?

parts.note: not inference but the measurement taken of the distance between two railway rails

explanation.definitionFit: A gauge is both a measuring instrument with a reading and the width between railway tracks.

clue.text: Noise to attract attention from ship's stern

indicators.note: from tells you to take the letters out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A sound made to get attention from the back of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across the end of ship's and the start of stern.
explanation.definitionFit: A whispered hiss used to catch someone's notice discreetly.

clue.text: Tied up this spring?

explanation.definitionFit: Both a past participle meaning fastened and a noun meaning a jump or leap.

clue.text: Endlessly pursue, tumble and seize

indicators.note: tumble means fall into disorder, so the remaining letters are jumbled
endlessly tells you to drop the final letter of the word pursue

explanation.surface: Keep chasing without end, fall over, and grab hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' cuts PURSUE to PURSU, and 'tumble' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: To usurp is to take power or position by force.

clue.text: One attracting buyers of light sideboard?

parts.note: a light is a window pane
a dresser is a sideboard with shelves for dishes

explanation.surface: Someone luring purchasers of a pale piece of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' is a noun meaning a window, not a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop staffer arranges goods in the shopfront display to draw in customers.

clue.text: Met tennis upset with feeling

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Encountered an emotional tennis upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges the nine letters of MET and TENNIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentiment is an emotion or attitude.

clue.text: Assorted donuts enlarge his patient quota

definitions.text: Assorted donuts enlarge his patient quota

indicators.note: assorted means mixed, so the letters of the two words are mixed together

explanation.surface: Sugary snacks boost the number of patients a dentist will have.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assorted' rearranges DONUTS and ENLARGE; the whole clue also describes the answer, since sweet treats rot teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A tooth specialist gains more work when people eat sweet things.

clue.text: This drawer is always untidy!

parts.note: not a messy furniture drawer but a person who draws aimless scribbles

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who scribbles idly produces messy little sketches.

clue.text: Saving company in money trouble?

indicators.note: in places the company abbreviation inside the jumbled letters
trouble suggests disturbance, so the letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: Asks whether a firm is saving because it has money problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges the money into ENOMY, and 'in' sets the company abbreviation after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Economy is careful avoidance of spending, thrift.

clue.text: Othello's retirement chamber

indicators.note: retirement means withdrawing or going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a room is a chamber

explanation.surface: The Shakespearean general's bedroom for going to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' reverses ROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Othello is subtitled the Moor of Venice.

clue.text: Song-thrush, male, the French notice

parts.note: avis is French for notice or announcement

explanation.surface: A list: a bird, a man, and a French notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Mavis is an old poetic name for the song thrush.

clue.text: Getting a four in grass, rotate the body

indicators.note: in puts the Roman numeral inside the slang word

parts.note: pot and grass are both slang for cannabis
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Scoring a boundary on the grass, a cricketer twists round.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a four is a boundary hit, which colours the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To pivot is to turn on a fixed point.

clue.text: Places I pass, going the wrong way

indicators.note: going the wrong way means travelling backwards, so the joined pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: Positions passed by someone travelling in the wrong direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going the wrong way' reverses ICOL, the letter I with COL.
explanation.definitionFit: Loci is the plural of locus, Latin for place or position.

clue.text: A sensation to be put up as a soap opera?

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means written bottom to top, so the joined pieces are read upwards

parts.note: a gas is something sensational or great fun

explanation.surface: Asks whether a sensational story could be staged as a soap opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' reverses AGAS, A plus GAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long, rambling story with many episodes, like a serial drama.

clue.text: Thin sort of clue, this

indicators.note: sort here means to arrange, so the letters of thin are sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: A weak kind of crossword clue, this one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges THIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A hint is a small suggestion or pointer toward a solution.

clue.text: Most booed player of football team at home?

parts.note: Villa is Aston Villa, the Birmingham football club
in means at home

explanation.surface: Asks which home-side footballer gets the most boos.
explanation.walkthrough: Aston Villa is an English football club usually shortened to Villa.
explanation.definitionFit: In a melodrama the bad guy is the character the audience hisses at.

clue.text: Typical example of English religious book

parts.note: pi is short for pious, meaning religious
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: A model instance of an English devotional volume.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome is a perfect representative of a type.

clue.text: Minor burn that runs?

parts.note: not a small injury from fire but a little Scottish brook that flows

explanation.definitionFit: Burn is the Scottish word for a brook, and a small flowing brook is a rivulet.

clue.text: Meeting-place, secret enough to test saint

parts.note: to try is to test

explanation.surface: A clandestine rendezvous, discreet enough to put a saint to the test.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a secret lovers' rendezvous or its location.
